where: Penumbra Ring + Starwell (the last dark before the Umbral Spire)
mood: Wall of Ink: the last dark, crossed on starlight; a held breath, your heartbeat and one lonely lamp-note, hope leaking in at the edges.
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
dark slow-shifting synth fog pad, slightly detuned
a sparse soft heartbeat kick every two bars
one lonely low square-wave lead note swelling out of the dark
oppressive hush with a fragile thread of hope
haunting slow three-note rising figure as the hook
spacious and sparse but clearly composed

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {out of near-silence a low D drone breathes in, one soft heartbeat kick, and a single lonely pulse-wave note rises and hangs in the dark like a lamp held up}

sections.name: Wall of Ink
sections.text: {the fog pad shifts slowly over the pedal drone; the lone lead plays a slow, haunting three-note rising figure that reaches up and stops short, unanswered; heartbeat kick every two bars}

sections.name: Lamp in the Dark
sections.text: {the same rising figure again a step higher, now answered by a faint echoing bell tone far off, the pad darkening underneath, the heartbeat a little nearer}

sections.name: Hope at the Edges
sections.text: {contrast: the drone lifts to F, the pad warms and its detune briefly settles, a tentative brighter phrase creeps upward like the wall receding a wedge, then the dark closes back in}

sections.name: Wall Returns
sections.text: {the dark D minor fog returns with the lonely rising figure; the last bar hangs on an unresolved A over the drone that leads straight back into the start of the theme}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme

_note: 2026-10 retro + tempo pass: motif dropped (it pinned the take to ~90 BPM); era-first anchor, retro kit/bass; opening shape chosen per scene.
